newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian PM says crisis has to be overcome.
newsitem.headline: Albanian PM says crisis has to be overcome.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino said on Tuesday it was important his country avoided a slide back into chaos and that he would hold talks with European security envoy Franz Vranitzky.

Fino, returning from a visit to Washington, walked into the middle of new turmoil for his country after President Sali Berisha said he would call elections for the end of June although most parties have threatened to boycott the vote.
"I think we have to overcome this crisis. We should talk with Vranitzky after his arrival today or tomorrow, with President Berisha and with the political parties," Fino told Albanian Television.

The elections are a vital element in plans to restore stability in Albania after the country was riven by riots and lawlessness in February and March after the collapse of high-yielding pyramid savings schemes cost thousands of people their life savings.
Vranitzky, who has been brokering the political talks, was preparing for his second trip to Albania in a week, hoping to defuse the fresh crisis. He was to arrive on Thursday morning.

Fino's Socialist Party and the rest of an interim Government of Reconciliation have said they will not stand in the elections after Berisha's Democratic Party passed an election law which the parties said favoured the Democrats.
Fino said his trip to the U.S. was a success and that his government had the support of the U.S. and Vranitzky.

"Their reaction (the U.S. State Department and Vranitzky) was positive because this Government of National Reconciliation should be protected, the problems should be resolved and I think the problems will be resolved together," he added.
